'''Awngthim''' is an [[Language death|extinct]] [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] formerly spoken in [[Cape York Peninsula|Cape York]] in [[Queensland]], [[Australia]] by the [[Winduwinda|Winduwinda people]]. The Awngthim language region includes the areas around Weipa and the Cook Shire.<ref name=":SLQ129">{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/129?embed=true|title=Thaynakwith|publisher=[[State Library of Queensland]]|website=Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages map|url-status=live|accessdate=6 June 2022}}</ref>

==Name==
The name ''Awngthim'' is not a synonym of ''[[Anguthimri language|Anguthimri]]'', though due to their similarity they have sometimes been confused.<ref>{{cite web|title=Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code|publisher=ISO 639-3 Registration Authority|access-date=28 December 2022|url=http://www.sil.org/iso639-3/cr_files/2011-137.pdf}}</ref>

==Dialects==
Hale (1964) treats Awngthim as a cover term for dialects Ntrwa'ngayth {{IPA|/ntʳwaʔŋajt̪/}}, Thyanhngayth {{IPA|/t̪jan̪ŋajt̪/}}, and Mamngayth {{IPA|/mamŋajt̪/}}.<ref name=":hale1964">{{cite journal |last1=Hale |first1=Kenneth |date=1964 |title=Classification of Northern Paman Languages, Cape York Peninsula, Australia: A Research Report |journal=Oceanic Linguistics |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=248–265 |doi=10.2307/3622881|jstor=3622881 }}</ref>  ''-Ngayth'' is a suffix common to many tribal names of the area. These are the Ntrwa'a, Thyanh, and Mam dialects.

The [[Ndrangith language|Ndrangith]] and [[Ndra'ngith language|Ndra'ngith]] languages have been confused with Ntrwa'ngayth.
